Let $A = \left(\begin{array}{ccc} -4 & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10 & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14 \end{array}\right)$. The characteristic polynomial is given by $p_A(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I)$, where $I$ is the identity matrix. So we have
\begin{align*} \label{eq:1} A - \lambda I = \left(\begin{array}{ccc} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{array}\right)\end{align*}
The determinant is
\begin{align*} p_A(\lambda) &= \det(A - \lambda I) \\ &= (-4-\lambda) \left[(10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (-5)(4)\right] \\ & \quad - (-13) \left[(-9)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(12)\right] \\ & \quad + (10) \left[(-9)(-5) - (12)(10-\lambda)\right] \\ &= (-4-\lambda) \left[-140 - 10\lambda + 14\lambda + \lambda^2 + 20\right] \\ & \quad + 13 \left[126 + 9\lambda - 48\right] \\ & \quad + 10 \left[45 - 120 + 12\lambda\right] \\ &= (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(78 + 9\lambda) + 10(-75 + 12\lambda) \\ &= -4(\lambda^2+4\lambda-120) - \lambda(\lambda^2+4\lambda-120) + 1014 + 117\lambda - 750 + 120\lambda \\ &= -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda + 1014 + 117\lambda - 750 + 120\lambda \\ &= -\lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 - 4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 120\lambda + 117\lambda + 120\lambda + 480 + 1014 - 750 \\ &= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744\end{align*}
Therefore,
$$ p_A(\lambda) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$$

Final Answer: The final answer is $\boxed{-\lambda^3 - 8 \lambda^2 + 341 \lambda + 744}$
